sources.note: The September 2026 application covers initial family and group-home licensing. Current guidance limits initial group-home licences to up to 12 spaces; later expansion beyond 12 has additional conditions. Original check handling is confirmed with the consultant.

sources.note: Applicant responses and consultant assessment are distinct parts of suitability review.

sources.title: Centre community needs assessment
sources.note: Published submission channel: cwcentredev@gov.sk.ca. Requests entity details, spaces by age, community need and financial readiness.

sources.title: Centre licence application form
sources.note: Return to the ELCC consultant. Published form includes consultant, manager and director decision fields; older form details must be checked against current regulations.

sources.title: The Child Care Act, 2014 — current consolidation
sources.note: Sections 2 and 5–8 distinguish settings, licensing and applicant eligibility, including current 2026 amendments.

sources.title: Group Family Child Care Home Providers — September 2026

decisionHelp.readiness: Readiness is a proposed administrative checkpoint. It does not authorize operation.
decisionHelp.licence: Only the Ministry can issue an operating licence and set its conditions.
decisionHelp.funding: Space allocation and grant approvals require separate Ministry decisions. A licence does not guarantee funding.

workflow.currentProcedure: The published process includes information sessions, application review, consultant visits, inspections and a licensing decision. Centre development and funding have additional approval steps.
workflow.prototypeProcedure: This prototype groups the work into four stages and one facility record. Shared documents, correction threads and visible progress are proposed improvements.
workflow.submissionNotice: This local demonstration does not submit an application, contact officials, issue a licence or award funding.
workflow.originalCheckHandling: Record delivery and Ministry verification of original checks separately. Uploading a scan does not satisfy the published sealed-original requirement.
workflow.dataNotice: All cases and progress shown here are fictional. Do not enter real criminal-record, health, identity or banking information.
workflow.decisionNotice: Staff review remains necessary. No automated eligibility, suitability, licensing or funding decisions are made.
workflow.existingSystems: The Ministry already uses an Enrolment Portal for fee schedules. This prototype proposes a connected applicant experience; it does not imply that every current step is paper-based.

facilityTypes.title: Family child care home
facilityTypes.currentProcedure: Information session, application package, local-need screening, learning sessions, home visits, inspections and final licensing review.
facilityTypes.capacityNote: Normally up to eight attending children, including resident children, within age-combination and licence limits.
facilityTypes.fundingNote: Regulation can provide access to grants; each applicable approval still needs confirmation.
afterLicensing: Introductory ECE training within one year, subject to the regulatory exemption.
At least six hours of continuing education annually.
CPR within six months if it was not included in the first-aid course.
facilityTypes.eligibilityNote: Home licence applicants must be individuals aged 18 or older who reside in Saskatchewan.

facilityTypes.title: Group family child care home
facilityTypes.currentProcedure: Home licensing pathway plus review of assistants, staffing, child ages and the requested group-home capacity.
facilityTypes.capacityNote: New group family homes may initially be licensed for up to 12 spaces. Existing group homes with at least two years on a regular licence may apply for up to 16 in targeted need areas, subject to premises, age mix and Ministry approval. An assistant is needed whenever numbers or ages exceed the family-home limits.
facilityTypes.fundingNote: Space and grant approvals are separate decisions; local demand can affect whether development proceeds.
afterLicensing: Introductory ECE training within one year, subject to the regulatory exemption.
Group-home licensee must meet ECE I qualifications within three years.
At least six hours of continuing education annually.
facilityTypes.eligibilityNote: Home licence applicants must be individuals aged 18 or older who reside in Saskatchewan.

facilityTypes.title: Child care centre
facilityTypes.currentProcedure: Development information session and needs assessment with budgets, Ministry review, applicable development/funding agreements, licence application, premises and operational review, then licensing decision.
facilityTypes.capacityNote: A centre licence sets capacity and age allocations; the regulatory maximum is 90 spaces.
facilityTypes.fundingNote: Licensing and funding have different eligibility. The published centre funding programme requires an eligible non-profit, co-operative or municipal entity; for-profit operations are not eligible for that funding.
afterLicensing: Maintain required staffing, qualification, insurance and operating standards.
Use the existing Ministry reporting channels for enrolment and fee information.
facilityTypes.eligibilityNote: Centre applicants may be eligible corporations, co-operatives, municipalities, adult Saskatchewan residents or partnerships of adult Saskatchewan residents. Structure-specific ownership conditions apply; funding has separate eligibility.

documentTypes.title: Applicant information session
documentTypes.note: Record completion; this is not a suitability decision.
documentTypes.requirement: Before submitting the initial home application

documentTypes.title: Community needs assessment
documentTypes.note: Published form is emailed to the centre development team.

documentTypes.title: Development and operating budgets
documentTypes.note: Show expected development costs, operating income and expenses.

documentTypes.title: Applicant organization and ownership records
documentTypes.note: Grant eligibility requires a non-profit corporation, co-operative or municipality. For-profit licensing is a separate route.
documentTypes.requirement: Corporate registration and ownership records when applying as a corporation or co-operative.

documentTypes.title: Licence application
documentTypes.note: Use the home application for family and group-family homes; use the separate centre application for a centre.

documentTypes.title: Family assessment questionnaire
documentTypes.note: Applicant responses and consultant assessment remain separate.

documentTypes.title: Original applicant and adult-household checks
documentTypes.note: Track each required original criminal-record/vulnerable-sector check and Ministry verification. Do not store check contents in this demo.

documentTypes.title: Four character references
documentTypes.note: Track completion only; no real reference identities in this demo.

documentTypes.title: Payment setup
documentTypes.note: Separate payment setup from the licensing decision. No banking details in this demo.

documentTypes.title: Fire inspection report
documentTypes.note: For homes, the consultant advises when to arrange the inspection.

documentTypes.title: Facility insurance
documentTypes.note: Review required liability, personal-injury and transport coverage against the proposed operation.

documentTypes.title: Home space and outdoor-play review
documentTypes.note: The consultant checks usable space, play arrangements and the proposed child mix.

documentTypes.title: Approved centre floor plan
documentTypes.note: Approval is recorded by the responsible reviewer; an upload alone is not approval.

documentTypes.title: Signed lease, if premises are rented
documentTypes.requirement: Signed lease when premises are rented.

documentTypes.title: Home first-aid and training plan
documentTypes.note: First aid is required. If it omits CPR, CPR must follow within six months of licensing. Introductory ECE training is due within one year; do not incorrectly make all later training a pre-licence condition.

documentTypes.title: Group-home assistant and staffing review
documentTypes.note: Review assistants, checks, training, child ages and capacity. The maximum alone does not determine permitted staffing.

documentTypes.title: Centre staffing and qualifications
documentTypes.note: Review director and worker qualifications, required checks and supervision arrangements.

documentTypes.title: Operating policies and agreements
documentTypes.note: Required operational and child-management policies and parent service agreements; centres also prepare parent and staff handbooks.

documentTypes.title: Centre menu, governance and fee records
documentTypes.note: Includes board/advisory information and menu. The official checklist sends fee schedules through the existing Enrolment Portal.

documentTypes.title: Final consultant review
documentTypes.note: The centre checklist calls for a final meeting at least four weeks before anticipated opening; this is not an approval-time promise.

documentTypes.title: Operating-licence decision
documentTypes.note: Record the issued licence and conditions only after an authorized Ministry decision.

documentTypes.title: Space-allocation and funding records
documentTypes.note: Track allocation and grant outcomes separately. A completed document checklist is not a funding approval.
documentTypes.requirement: Only where allocation or funding is requested

documentTypes.title: Private operator criminal-record check
documentTypes.requirement: Private-operator check where applicable; confirm handling with the consultant.
documentTypes.note: Track completion only; do not store check contents in this prototype.
